This classroom has become so quiet? So all of us are graduates now? Oh well, it has been quite a journey for me, reading post after post, seeing how people overcame their struggles, confusions, self-doubts, pain inflicted by Market. I honestly think that there are a few loose pieces that needs to be tighten up. Perhaps it's to do with my profession - I am not a perfectionist but I like to be exact and precise about definition. So let's sort out any confusion regarding FTR vs FL once for all, agree?

In case people still wonder what's FTR and what's FL. Let this diagram clear the confusion, and I am not inventing something new, I am just applying what I have learned from the articles in Marketpedia

FTR = Failure to Return. I would actually prefer a more precise technical term. Because Failure to Return can be applied on any Fresh SD zones, i.e. after a zone is created, price has not returned to test it, so arguably any Fresh level = Failure to Return.

The definition of FTR vs FL, according to the Marketpedia articles can be summarized in the following diagram:

So essentially, an FL is created AFTER breaking a key barrier, and FL is drawn from Point 1 to Point 2. Where FTR is the MPL of the FL on this SAME TIMEFRAME.

The next question I see many people have asked is, where do we look for trades? Is it at DP (decision to break), or at FL, or at FTR?

MasterTrader Harry, basically put this to rest. according to him, - If after the creation of FL, price comes back to test the FL within a short period of time, then the FL has a high chance of turning price around. - However, if price does not come back, instead it leaves the area and go on a significant consolidation period, by the time it comes to this area, the FL is no longer a reliable trade location.

So here is my takeaway from Harry's words: if price comes back after a long consolidation period away from the area, I would look at the FL as a FO level, and pay attention to the DP just beyond it as the area that has higher chance of turning price.

I have also seen the word DP (Decision Point) causing confusion, because based on normal English definition, a DP is just Decision Point, and open up any charts, every point on the chart is a decision, every second there are decision to buy and sell by market participants. But in the spirit of RTM, my understanding is that DP is the 'kink' or 'pause' BEFORE the break of a key barrier. Whereas FL is the 'kink' AFTER the break of a barrier.

So DP = Kink, FL = Kink, FTR = Kink but in a lower time scale than the parent FL.

So a 'kink' is one of the most important revelation for me! When I see kinks, I see $$$$, All Hail the KINK! So what is a kink? Perhaps this video can explain better than I do

Thank you all. RTM has been a great home and a great retreat for me. AK

Hi Einrikr, your statement that kink A is unimportant raise a question. And that's to do with creation of 'kink'. Take this diagram below, would you consider B the LS kink? I purposely drew the kink small to signify that we need to go a least several TF lower to see it.

Base on my understanding of the RTM materials so far, a kink is created after breaking another kink to its left. By this reasoning, kink A is important because the break of it creates kink B.

On the other hand, a kink is also said to be created after breaking an SR. But what is an SR? In RTM, we draw SR as horizontal line. So, what if we have the following scenario, which one is the LS kink, B or C?

I have also heard the term "To-The-Pip" Kink, and in video 2 of RTMA Lite, I heard IF mentioning briefly that C is the so-called "To-the-Pip" Kink.

THANKS. AK

However, as far as I've understood RTM materials, a LS is created due to RS (or, for that matter, due to a kink on RS level) and creates a kink on that very same level so you should always look for your LSK at C. The kink at A is already broken and B is an insignificant kink for your LS so you should go for C. But as I said, I've just been going over RTM materials for 2 weeks now and to be brutally honest, I have been in the trading business for only a few months so I might be a bit "bleu", so if I'm wrong about this, please feel free to say so!

I guess I'll call it a day, take the dog for another walk and have a couple of beers to let it all sink in. I think I'm on track with all this kink-stuff but there's lots more to learn. One last thing: I feel like RS is not a straight line per se, but moves like this:

When we looking at LS, we might be missing symmetry in market. so when price makes PA on another end of symmetry, It will retrace back till Last symmetry where LS was which might become QM.

I was studying your diagram and narrative AK and my take on it is this. A DP (Decision Point) is just a term that was used in place of FL before the FL terminology was developed (as per the Markepedia Topic on Flag Limits). For your explanation in this post I don't believe it is relevant to have the DP on there. A kink below a Barrier I don't believe is a decision to break just because there is a kink there, unless I am missing something from the Markepedia articles. Your DP on the diagram could be a kink from the break of a Barrier further to the left, then it may become important later on if price returns.

I also have a slightly different understanding on FTR v FL v MPL. Please see my chart below for my understanding and explanation.

With regards to where we should look for trades, I'm by no means anywhere near that as yet however, my current understanding is that we can look to multiple areas within the FL (see point 4 on my chart).

Cheers,
